top.description: BINGHAMTON, NY - MAY 26: Franklin Arias #50 of the Portland Sea Dogs celebrates with teammates after defeating the Binghamton Rumble Ponies at Mirabito Stadium on Tuesday, May 26, 2026 in Binghamton, New York. top.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is taking fewer shots than ever before in his long career, yet the Philadelphia 76ers are winning more games than any other team in the league. Through his first seven games, the four-time champion is averaging 15.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 7.4 assists. His field-goal attempts have dropped to just 13.1 per game, while his free-throw attempts sit at 4.4. These numbers mark the lowest pace for his scoring average and shot volume since he entered the NBA as a rookie. Instead of carrying the offense alone, James is now playing as a facilitator alongside a roster packed with elite scorers. On Wednesday night, Detroit Pistons fell 112-106 as the 76ers secured eight wins from their opening nine contests. This surprising drop in personal usage has allowed Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown to generate offense independently while James directs the flow. Defense Becomes the Team Identity While James cuts back on his scoring, the starting five has limited opponents’ scoring. The group has held teams to just 95.4 points per 100 possessions across their first five games together. For context, the league’s best defense before Thursday was allowing 103 points per 100 possessions. This gap shows how much the Sixers have improved on that end of the floor. James made the goal clear after the win over Detroit. After defeating the Pistons on Wednesday, “Our defense is going to be our identity,” James stated, according to NBC News . The starting lineup features James, Brown, Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe, and Joel Embiid, a group that combines for 36 All-Star selections. They have outscored opponents by 15 points in 77 minutes of play together. During 11 Cleveland seasons, he guided the franchise to its initial 2016 NBA championship. The Cavaliers enter Friday with a 4-4 record after back-to-back losses to Oklahoma City. They also face injury concerns with key player Jarrett Allen listed as questionable for tonight’s game. Donovan Mitchell has averaged 22.5 points for Cleveland, but the team needs better collective production to beat Philadelphia. James Harden has struggled with his shooting efficiency. With the Eastern Conference’s top record, the 76ers have claimed five straight victories. James noted that his role has changed because he knows the team needs him to be ready for late-game situations. top.title: ‘Looks play a big part’: Former WNBA star explains why Sophie Cunningham is popular despite lackluster stats
top.description: Aug 23, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) reacts while warming up prior to a game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Caitlin Clark has become the face of the WNBA, and the Indiana Fever have become one of the league’s most popular teams because of her. But WNBA legend Angel McCoughtry thinks Clark’s teammate Kelsey Mitchell isn’t getting nearly enough credit. Appearing on the Get To The Point podcast with Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer, McCoughtry argued that looks play a bigger role in WNBA marketing than they do in other sports. She pointed to Mitchell as an example, saying that the Fever’s “best player” is barely recognized by fans. Mitchell’s Big Season Mitchell put together a terrific season for the Fever in 2026. She led the team in scoring, averaging 24.7 points per game, while Clark averaged 22.3 points per game. Mitchell has also been one of Indiana’s most consistent players in recent years, earning All-Star honors and serving as the Fever’s top scoring threat alongside Clark. Still, Clark is the one who draws the crowds and the endorsements. Her arrival turned the Fever into a national draw, and she has become one of the most marketable athletes in sports. ‘Looks play a big part’ McCoughtry, a five-time WNBA All-Star, said that she noticed the gap in attention firsthand. “In the NFL and NBA, if you’re good, you’re good. In the WNBA, if you look pretty… You might not be the best player…” McCoughtry said. “I went to a conference, and everybody loved Indiana. They love Caitlin Clark. I said, ‘How many of you know Kelsey Mitchell?’ None of them raised their hand. She’s the best player on the team,” McCoughtry said, on the podcast . “The leading scorer on that team. Only 100k. She don’t have a million followers.” Owens jumped in to ask if McCoughtry was suggesting that Clark is pretty. She declined to say that she was, but she then brought up Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, pointing out that she has an Adidas shoe deal despite averaging “nine points per game.” Cunningham actually averaged 7.9 points per game this season. McCoughtry said that there are other girls that are “balling” that don’t have similar deals. “Not the best player you’ve ever seen, but she’s getting the brand endorsements,” McCoughtry said. “In the woman’s game, is it really about how good you are or the visibility – how pretty you are?” “Yes, looks play a part. They play a big part,” McCoughtry said. Spencer went on to bring up other examples like Anna Kournikova and Michelle Wei, who weren’t the most successful in their sport but received brand sponsorships, potentially because of their looks. top.title: Gateway Dirt Nationals Best Appearing Car Contest Returns In 2026 With Cash Prizes
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The 2026 Gateway Dirt Nationals will give fans a direct say in which race cars look the best on the track. Organizers confirmed that the Best Appearing Car Contest returns this year for both the Super Late Model and Modified divisions. Two drivers will walk away with cash prizes, and the crowd gets to pick the winners. FloRacing and the event organizers plan to hand out $1,000 to the winner in each division. The money might seem small compared to the race purse, but the bragging rights are worth much more to the teams. Tyler Carpenter won the Super Late Model title in 2026, while Haleigh Gross took the award in the Modified class, according to FloRacing . Now the competition resets for a new year of paint jobs and creative designs. A Decade of Indoor Racing The race takes place inside The Dome at America’s Center, a venue that has hosted the event for ten years. This setting allows for unique paint schemes that might not survive on outdoor tracks. Drivers and teams arrive each December with eye-catching designs to grab the attention of the crowd. The contest celebrates this decade of racing indoors by rewarding the teams that put the most effort into their look. They will select 10 cars from each division to become finalists before the public votes. This step ensures that only the most impressive rides make it to the final round. Photo galleries featuring all 20 finalists will appear on FloRacing so fans can see the details up close. How the Voting Works Once the finalists are announced, the fans take control of the outcome. Supporters can visit FloRacing.com to cast their votes for their favorite cars. During the voting period, rules permit fans to cast up to four votes each day. This high volume of voting keeps the engagement high as the event gets closer. The specific dates for voting and other contest details will be released as the event approaches. FloRacing reported that the 2026 Kubota Gateway Dirt Nationals will bring Super Late Models and Modifieds indoors for three nights of racing in December. FloRacing will broadcast all three nights of racing live for viewers who cannot travel to St. Louis. A Massive Field of Drivers The race itself features a huge entry list that proves dirt racing is stronger than ever. top.title: NFL Rumors: Insider Sheds Light on Lamar Jackson’s Future with Baltimore Ravens
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a severe thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills in his first game back after missing multiple weeks with an ankle sprain. While Baltimore just acquired Jacoby Brissett to fill the void at quarterback for the rest of 2026, questions remain about Jackson’s future with the franchise. Baltimore must figure out something with Jackson this offseason. The 2027 NFL salary cap is currently projected by OverTheCap.com to be $327 million. Jackson’s cap hit next season is too high for the franchise to justify, especially given the needs throughout its roster with aspirations to rebound as a playoff contender. Lamar Jackson contract ( Spotrac ): $84.34 million cap hit in 2027, $42.47 million dead cap in 2028 Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta’s options are further complicated by the contract extension he signed his MVP quarterback to in 2023. Jackson’s five-year deal included a no-trade clause, meaning that Baltimore needs his explicit approval to move him to another club. The franchise also can’t use the franchise tag on him in 2028 when he expires. That gives Jackson, who doesn’t have an official agent, complete leverage over the situation. Many in sports media and around the National Football League have speculated that the two-time NFL MVP and the storied franchise could potentially part ways after the 2026 season. However, that doesn’t seem to be the plan. Ahead of Baltimore’s Week 8 Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Amazon Prime Video that the Ravens are willing to make Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history. When the Kansas City Chiefs reworked the Patrick Mahomes contract in June, the agreement added two years to his contract and made the average annual value a record-setting $64 million. Mahomes and Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott ($60 million AAV) are the only NFL players making $60-plus million per season. Ahead of his age-30 season, it stands to reason that Jackson would be looking for another five-year contract. Baltimore could tack four years onto his current deal, potentially at $65 million per season. It would make him the highest-paid player in NFL history, keep him under contract through his age-35 season and likely allow him to spend his entire career in a Ravens uniform. He never once won a Silver Slugger Award. Jay Bruce, Votto’s longtime sidekick during the best run of form the Cincinnati Reds have had at any point during the last 35 years, won a pair of Silver Slugger Awards in his career. Silver Sluggers are not exactly the most precise way to define hitting excellence. That said, they still carry weight among the players themselves, however, as they are voted on among managers and coaches league-wide to determine which players were the ‘best’ hitters at their own positions during the most recent season. The finalists at each position in both the National League and American League were announced on Friday, and both of Cincinnati’s best hitters from 2026 were among them. top.title: Tennessee’s key to beating Kentucky? Don’t beat yourself
top.description: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 12: Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel talks with a referee during the college football game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on September 12th, 2026 at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tennessee saw a golden opportunity to give themselves a cushion for the rest of the season two weeks ago in Columbia slip through their fingertips. The Volunteers found a way to lose against South Carolina as the mistakes finally caught up with them late. Tennessee was penalized 12 times for 90 yards against the Gamecocks, famously taking three passing touchdowns from George MacIntyre off the board. The penalties have been a theme for Tennessee ever since Josh Heupel arrived in Knoxville. Heupel’s Tennessee teams have finished outside of the top 100 overall in penalties in four of his five seasons. 2026 has been no different. The Volunteers rank 100th in FBS with 61 penalties on the year. They’re 91st in penalty yards, checking in with 62.12 yards surrendered per game. Tennessee’s opponent this week, Kentucky, is 17th in the same statistic. That’s been a theme for Kentucky all season long — playing clean and taking advantage of opportunities. It’s something that quarterback Kenny Minchey can hang his hat on this year, throwing 14 touchdowns against just one interception. Kentucky has a turnover margin of +13 for the season. Tennessee is +3 in that category for the season. The Volunteers have turned the ball over 11 times on the season, with an opportunistic, aggressive defense propping up their overall margin. Kentucky has turned the ball over just five times all season. “Playing a really good football team that is playing extremely well together,” Josh Heupel said of Kentucky. “You look at their ability to win multiple ways, finish games. Turnover margin, they’ve been elite. One of the least-penalized teams in the league, playing really smart all three phases, so it’ll be a great test.” With an inexperienced quarterback making just his fourth start, keeping things on schedule is a must. The little things — the 3rd and 3 that turns into 3rd and 8 — those are the things that Tennessee really can’t afford down the homestretch, starting on Saturday night. The Volunteers are playing a defensive, ball-control brand this season, and that brand really needs clean football to be successful. We’ll see if Tennessee can clean things up against Kentucky on Saturday. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

top.title: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan
top.description: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract that will keep him at AC Milan until 2031. It is a well-deserved renewal and a career-defining moment for the American winger. Christian Pulisic is staying put at AC Milan . The 28-year-old American winger will remain under contract with the Rossoneri until June 2031, earning a pay rise to €6.5 million net per year, with the figure potentially reaching €10 million if he achieves certain objectives. However you look at it, Pulisic is now one of AC Milan’s highest-paid players and among the top earners in Serie A , alongside Lautaro Martínez , Nicolò Barella, Kevin De Bruyne , and Kenan Yıldız . All of this comes on the heels of Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners and owner of AC Milan since August 2022, telling CBS Sports: “We have a connection. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to find our way and understand Italy. He’s Captain America, but he’s also my franchise player.” That is an important milestone for an American playing in Europe, particularly one who has already represented three major clubs. Today, Pulisic can look in the mirror and know that his career will be defined by his time at AC Milan, much like Clint Dempsey’s was defined by Fulham or Tim Howard’s by Everton . Pulisic is a Rossoneri player, and for American soccer, that is a remarkable achievement. Pulisic’s Numbers: Not Just Impressive, But a Benchmark The tale of the tape for Pulisic at AC Milan deserves a standing ovation at the San Siro : 45 goals and 28 assists in 144 games. He has also scored four goals against Inter in all competitions, which puts him ahead of Milan legends including Marco van Basten, George Weah, and Ronaldinho . At the UEFA Champions League level, Pulisic has scored five goals, one of which was an Olimpico against Club Brugge . nigeria.title: ADC chairmen demand Mark’s removal; threaten protest against INEC
nigeria.description: The National Executive Committee Chairmen Forum of the African Democratic Congress has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to remove Senator David Mark and members of his dissolved Interim National Working Committee from its portal, threatening a nationwide protest if the commission fails to comply with a court judgment on the party’s leadership crisis. The forum also demanded that INEC replace their names with those of Nafiu Bala Gombe and other party officials it considers legally recognised. It further urged the commission to reopen its portal to allow the ADC to conduct fresh primaries where necessary and upload its candidates for the 2027 general elections. The forum’s secretary, Kennedy Odion, made the demands while addressing journalists in Abuja on Friday, a day after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, nullified the Mark-led interim leadership of the party. Odion said the judgment invalidated decisions taken by the dissolved leadership, including the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate and the emergence of other candidates through its congresses and national convention. He said the ruling affirmed the forum’s position that the interim leadership was not constitutionally recognised. “We, the only legally recognised NEC members, accept in its entirety the judgment declaring our own Alhaji Nafiu Bala Gombe the authentic national chairman of the ADC. “Failure to comply with this latest judgment will leave us no option but to proceed with our planned nationwide protest against the electoral umpire. Nigeria is for all of us. No individual, however highly placed, is above the law,” he said. Odion also argued that the judgment invalidated the candidacies of Atiku, his running mate, former Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi, and other politicians who emerged through the interim leadership’s processes. The ADC has been divided by a prolonged leadership dispute between the Mark-led interim national working committee and the faction led by Bala Gombe. The crisis had earlier resulted in a Federal High Court judgment delivered by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik on April 29, 2026, which affirmed the tenure of elected state executive committees pending the conduct of valid congresses and a national convention. The court also restrained INEC from recognising congresses organised by the interim national working committee. The Court of Appeal upheld the decision on June 13, 2026. Odion alleged that despite the earlier rulings, INEC continued to recognise the Mark-led leadership and accept candidates produced through its congresses and convention. He said the forum had pursued legal remedies rather than confrontation, adding that its restraint had prevented violence among aggrieved party members. nigeria.title: I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Nwafor Sunday President Bola Tinubu has said he will spend the night in Akwa Ibom State, declaring that his visit is a “second term presidential sleep” as he expressed confidence in securing re-election in 2027. Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. Addressing the crowd, the President thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general election. “Thank you, Akwa Ibom. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. The weapon you have is the PVC. If you have not collected it, please go ahead and collect your PVC. I am begging you, for the sake of your future,” he said. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. The President’s declaration comes amid criticism from the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, who had taken a swipe at him over his travels across the country. Obi had suggested that Tinubu had not spent the night in any state outside Abuja and Lagos, a remark that appeared to question the President’s physical presence across the country. Tinubu’s announcement that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom comes against the backdrop of the exchange between the two political figures as political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum. nigeria.title: Lagos seals over 45 buildings in Eko, Ifako-Ijaiye
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Physical Planning Permit Authority (LASPPPA) has sealed more than 45 buildings in Eko and Ifako-Ijaiye districts over alleged violations of physical planning regulations. The enforcement exercises were carried out by the authority’s Monitoring and Compliance Unit on Wednesday in Ifako-Ijaiye District and Thursday in Eko District. In a statement shared on its Facebook page on Thursday, LASPPPA said 25 properties were sealed in Ifako-Ijaiye for operating without valid planning permits, excessive density, illegal remodelling, deviation from approved plans and ongoing construction without approval. In a separate update on Friday, the agency disclosed that more than 20 buildings were sealed in Eko District for various planning violations. It said 10 properties were found to have deviated from their approved building plans, while five were sealed for excessive density and another five for carrying out remodelling without the required permits. Other affected properties were sealed for undertaking construction work without planning approval. According to LASPPPA, the affected property owners and developers had earlier been served contravention notices by the respective district offices but failed to comply with the directives. “Contravention notices had been served by the district office previously, but compliance was not achieved,” the agency stated. The authority advised owners and developers of the affected properties to visit their nearest LASPPPA district office or its headquarters at Oba Akinjobi Way, GRA, Ikeja, for regularisation and further guidance. Meanwhile, a source in the agency, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said monitoring and enforcement of physical planning regulations were continuous exercises. nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the long-awaited Ibom Deep Seaport project in Akwa Ibom State following a request by Governor Umo Eno. Tinubu announced the approval on Friday while responding to the governor’s appeal during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. nigeria.title: Kenyan preacher sentenced to 200 years in prison over child murders
nigeria.description: A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for the murder of 190 children and one adult in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect’s base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the “Shakahola Forest Massacre”. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, was accused of inciting his followers to starve themselves to death to “meet Jesus”. He was convicted last month of murdering 191 people between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused. On Friday, the court sentenced him to 100 years for the homicide charges and 100 years for the starvation charges, while his accomplices — many of whom starved their own children to death — received a variety of lengthy prison terms. “Children observed siblings drop dead… as their parents ate and drank,” the judge said. “Some died as a result of strangulation, severely beaten… Children were subjected to extreme suffering… terrifying living conditions, psychological trauma.” Mackenzie was impassive as the sentence was read out, as he had been throughout the trial. Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, but the judge said it would “fail to achieve deterrence, particularly where the convicts regard death as a pathway to heaven and a union with Jesus and their deceased children.” Kenya has the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1987. Francis Wanje, a 62-year-old teacher who lost two grandchildren to the cult, told AFP he had hoped Mackenzie would be sentenced to death to prevent further tragedies. Another of his grandchildren, now 11, went without food for eight days before being rescued in March 2023. He testified that his brothers, aged two and five, had died after their parents, acting on the guru’s orders, forbade them from eating or drinking. “Nothing can ease the pain,” said Wanje, who blamed authorities for failing to act swiftly. “I really have great (anger) towards the authorities. If they had taken action, we would not be here today,” he added. – Death penalty – Mackenzie’s lawyer said he would appeal the verdict. He also faces manslaughter and terrorism charges in other trials, which he denies. Around 120 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial. According to witnesses, the movement denounced formal education as “satanic”, viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil and required followers to cut themselves off from the outside world. Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare (800-acre) ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya’s coast. nigeria.title: NDLEA remands two Mexicans, four Nigerians over Oyo meth lab
nigeria.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arraigned two Mexican nationals and four Nigerians over their alleged involvement in the establishment and operation of a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in Tapa village, Ibarapa North Local Government Area of Oyo State. The six defendants were arraigned before Justice Nkeonye Evelyn Maha of the Federal High Court, Ibadan, on a four-count charge bordering on conspiracy, drug trafficking and the illegal production of methamphetamine. The NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. The defendants are 56-year-old Mexican, Jose Villa Ochoa; another Mexican, Carrera Loaiza Arturo, 40; and four Nigerians identified as Maxwell Uche Nevoh, 30; Olatunji Yusuf, 37; Bankole Akeem Owolabi, 45; and Ganiu Monsiu, 43. According to the statement, NDLEA operatives arrested Ochoa and the four Nigerian defendants on June 17, 2026, in a forested area of Tapa village, while Arturo was arrested on August 19, 2026, at the Lagos airport while allegedly attempting to flee the country. Babafemi said the four-count charge accused the defendants of conspiring to operate a drug trafficking organisation and establishing a clandestine laboratory for the production of methamphetamine between December 2025 and June 2026 at different locations in Lagos and Oyo states. They were also accused of unlawfully transporting and distributing chemical substances intended for the manufacture of methamphetamine, contrary to Section 20(1)(f) and punishable under Section 20(2)(a) of the NDLEA Act. All six defendants pleaded not guilty when the charges were read to them. Following their pleas, Justice Maha ordered that they be remanded at the Correctional Centre in Ibadan. The case was adjourned until January 26, 27, 28 and 29, 2027, for trial. The NDLEA spokesman also disclosed that three other Mexican nationals and seven Nigerians arrested over a similar alleged operation at a forest hideout in Ogun State on May 16, 2026, had been remanded following their arraignment before a Federal High Court in Lagos. nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has announced plans to deploy about 2,000 additional Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure units across the country to accelerate adoption of the alternative fuel and reduce transportation costs. Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (PI-CNG/EV), Ismaeel Ahmed, disclosed this on Friday shortly after the commissioning of a Rolling Energy CNG refuelling station for the State House in Karu, Abuja. Ahmed said Nigeria currently had about 160 operational CNG refuelling stations, while another 170 were at various stages of development or awaiting approval from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). He said the programme had moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage, with private investors committing about $2.6 billion to the development of CNG infrastructure. According to him, President Bola Tinubu has directed a fresh round of infrastructure expansion involving 1,500 units in February and another 500 in August through the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the additional facilities were expected to become operational between this year and early next year. “This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven,” Ahmed said. He noted that Nigeria, with an estimated population of 220 million and about 12 million vehicles, needed to accelerate the deployment of refuelling facilities to meet growing demand. On the impact of CNG adoption on transportation costs, Ahmed said fares had dropped by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where CNG-powered buses operate. He cited the Kano-Katsina route, where passengers who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 could now travel for about N1,500 using CNG-powered buses. “It has significantly reduced about 30 to 40 per cent of transportation fees in the routes where CNG buses are ferrying,” he said. The PI-CNG/EV chairman, however, acknowledged that existing facilities were inadequate to meet national demand, adding that the government was working to extend CNG-powered transportation to more commercial routes and underserved communities. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Peter Fashedemi, said the commissioning of the facility demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to leading by example in adopting CNG as an alternative to petrol. He said the initiative had become particularly important following the removal of petrol subsidy, which increased transportation costs and made cheaper alternative fuels imperative. nigeria.title: Fani-Kayode disowns purported conferment of SCN rank
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, has disassociated himself from the purported conferment of the Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) rank, also known as Blue Silk, on him by the Nigerian Law Society (NLS). Fani-Kayode said he neither authorised nor personally approved the acceptance of the designation, describing the circumstances surrounding the conferment as an unfortunate administrative misjudgment. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Lizzy Okoji, the former Minister of Aviation said his representation at the event by members of his staff followed an invitation sent to his office by the society as part of his official engagements. He, however, clarified that neither his staff’s attendance nor any communication subsequently made on his behalf should be interpreted as his personal endorsement or acceptance of the designation. The statement said the circumstances surrounding the representation and the subsequent communication of acceptance were regrettable and occurred without any intention to misrepresent his personal position or professional convictions. Fani-Kayode also raised concerns about the legal and professional implications of the purported conferment, particularly in relation to the statutory framework regulating the legal profession in Nigeria and relevant judicial pronouncements on the conferment of professional ranks outside the established legal framework. Describing himself as a legal practitioner of more than 41 years, he said he would not knowingly engage in any conduct that violates the law, undermines the integrity of the legal profession or brings it into disrepute. He added that he belonged to a family with three generations of legal practitioners and remained committed to upholding the law, professional ethics and the established traditions of the legal profession. The envoy said his clarification was intended to put his position on record, dispel misconceptions arising from the incident and reaffirm his commitment to the rule of law and the dignity of the legal profession. nigeria.title: Four dead, 14 critically ill after suspected herbal poisoning in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi At least four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are receiving treatment in hospital after consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. The incident reportedly followed the sale of herbal preparations by three men identified as Alhaji Mai Magamani, Mohamed and Musa Kolo to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju last weekend. An eyewitness said the incident came to light on Monday, November 2, 2026, after several residents who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations began experiencing similar symptoms. According to the eyewitness, the first victim reportedly died on Tuesday morning, while the second died in the early hours of Wednesday. Two others subsequently died on November 4. The source added that more than 14 other persons were receiving treatment, with several reportedly in critical condition. The three men allegedly involved in selling the herbal preparations were reportedly apprehended by the Igede Youth Council in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership and handed over to the police. The eyewitness said the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters had transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command for further investigation. Speaking during the handover of the suspects, President of the Igede Youth Council, Comrade John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State Government to ensure a thorough investigation and that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. Ozzidi said members of the community had resisted taking the law into their own hands, choosing instead to allow the police and other relevant authorities to handle the matter. He urged political officeholders from the area to monitor the investigation to ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were established and justice served. Contacted, Chairman of Oju Local Government Council, Mr Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he had yet to establish the exact number of fatalities. He said three deaths had been reported to him as of the previous day, while other affected persons were receiving treatment at the General Hospital, Oju. “My people are working on that. My security secretary, secretary and the security adviser are on it. “The others are in the General Hospital, Oju. My health department is also taking care of them. I have tried to calm the situation down. The person selling the herbs has been arrested and sent to Makurdi three days back,” he said. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to enquiries as of the time of filing this report. nigeria.title: Tinubu: We’ll turn stability into prosperity through enterprise
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s next economic priority is to translate the gains of ongoing reforms into prosperity through enterprise, industrial growth and expanded trade. Tinubu spoke on Thursday at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos. The President, represented by the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, said the Federal Government had made significant progress in stabilising the economy, adding that attention must now shift to stimulating production, creating jobs and expanding business opportunities. “The emergency is over. The foundation has been repaired. Our task now is to turn stability into prosperity, and enterprise is at the heart of that task,” he said. Highlighting the administration’s economic achievements, Tinubu said Nigeria’s gross external reserves rose to approximately $55.07 billion in October 2026, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves exceeded $40 billion, compared with less than $4 billion in 2023. He also noted that inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, while the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, describing the figures as evidence of improving economic fundamentals. On trade, the President said non-oil exports exceeded $6.1 billion in 2025, while capital importation reached about $21 billion. He expressed optimism that Nigerian businesses could leverage the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to access wider markets across the continent. However, he stressed that sustainable economic growth must be driven by domestic production and value addition rather than dependence on imports. Tinubu said the National Industrial Policy provided a roadmap for strengthening manufacturing, deepening local value chains and converting the country’s raw materials into finished products. He disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment and its agencies supported more than 115,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in 2025. He assured business owners of continued government efforts to improve their access to finance, electricity and markets. The President described industrial and trade policies as complementary, explaining that while industry provides goods for export, trade creates markets for locally manufactured products. He also welcomed exhibitors from more than 20 countries to the fair, announcing that Nigeria would host the Intra-African Trade Fair for the first time in 2027, in partnership with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank). The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. business.title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2% Strive reported $474.8 million of net income attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, a print that arrived Friday alongside a company claim that Class A total return had outperformed bitcoin by 103.7% year to date through the same date. GAAP net income was $509.0 million, or $5.24 a share on a fully diluted basis. Almost all of that came from a $533.7 million unrealized gain on digital assets marked to fair value. Operating revenue for the quarter was just $2.7 million, so the earnings line is a treasury mark, not a fee business. In a post on X that led with the outperformance figure, Strive also highlighted a year-to-date bitcoin yield of 63.2% and a bitcoin dollar gain of $9.00 per assumed diluted share outstanding, both measured through Sept. 30. Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole tied those metrics to the stock’s relative showing against the asset. “Strive has continued to successfully execute on its treasury management strategy, delivering a strong bitcoin yield year to date in 2026, which I believe is the primary driver of our common equity’s outperformance relative to Bitcoin so far this year,” Cole said in the earnings release. Bitcoin yield, buys and the preferred stack Bitcoin yield, as Strive defines it, is the percentage change in bitcoin per share over a period — not a cash yield. On that measure the company posted 18.5% in the third quarter alone and 19.3% from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30, after the SATS preferred debut. Strive acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter at an average cost of about $78,885 and 20,373 bitcoin over the nine months ended Sept. 30. Another 15,124 coins followed between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and 43,124 by Oct. 30, keeping Strive among the largest public corporate stacks after recent multi-thousand-coin buys and smaller weekly adds that still trailed Strategy . The capital stack that funded the buys is mostly perpetual preferreds. business.title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to. JUST IN: The White House is now reviewing a new rule which will allow Americans to invest in crypto through their 401(k) retirement plans pic.twitter.com/uXGGIXEzdC — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What the DOL safe harbor covers President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies. The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.” That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard. Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute. business.title: Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Why XRP and bitcoin matter here Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. business.title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported . Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated. Bitcoin price reaction Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing. CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause. Tech rout aftermath and ETF outflows Thursday’s session still sets the floor under the bitcoin price. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported . The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep. Bitcoin has traded with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year, so a correction in the Nasdaq has pulled the bitcoin price lower even when on-chain flows looked steady. business.title: South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. business.title: Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto,” a 2.4-meter, multi-dimensional cube, was presented on October 29 at Polo Dot as part of the Open Fest of LABITCONF 2026 . Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the Premio B·Arte, the work combines art, technology, and education in a journey through Bitcoin’s fundamental principles. The inauguration featured guided remarks by Rodolfo Andragnes and a musical performance by Mayumaná, according to an announcement by the organization. Buenos Aires now has a monument dedicated to Satoshi Nakamoto, the person—or group of people—behind the creation of Bitcoin, whose identity remains unknown. Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the fifth edition of the Premio B·Arte, the monument was conceived not only as a tribute to Satoshi, but also as an artistic and educational experience. Through its five faces—four lateral and one upper—it proposes a journey to approach different concepts that explain Bitcoin’s origin, functioning, and philosophy. During the inauguration, Rodolfo Andragnes — co-founder of Bitcoin.ar and LABITCONF — accompanied the public with words and explanations about the details of the work, guiding the reading of its various elements and the meaning behind each representation. The presentation was accompanied by a musical show by Mayumaná, which added rhythm and sound to the opening of this new space dedicated to Bitcoin’s history. Five faces to discover Bitcoin’s history and principles Each of the monument’s faces offers a gateway to a different aspect of Bitcoin. The figure of Satoshi Nakamoto, for example, represents the anonymous character of its creator and the collective dimension of a technology that, once set in motion, continued to grow thanks to thousands of people distributed around the world. The reflections and multiplied geometric forms also evoke the structure of a network that replicates and expands. Another of its faces addresses Bitcoin’s programmed scarcity through a cube that successively divides into halves in a Fibonacci sequence. The representation refers to “the halving”, the mechanism that approximately every four years halves the reward miners receive for validating blocks and that regulates the issuance of new bitcoins. Starting at 50 bitcoins per block, the total reward gets cut in half every four years for roughly 130 years, until 21 million bitcoins have been emitted and the block reward becomes zero. This supply limit is iconic to the cryptocurrency and key to its qualities as hard money. The work also incorporates the first words of Bitcoin’s foundational document, the white paper published by Satoshi Nakamoto in October 31st, 2008. There, the possibility of making electronic payments directly between people, without needing to go through a financial institution, is proposed. entertainment.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
entertainment.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. entertainment.description: From November 5 to 8, 2026 , Lagos will become the epicenter of African creativity as Afrique Femme brings the 6th edition of the Brunch des AfricanWoman2.0 to CANEX WKND 2026 at the iconic Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts. Organized by Afreximbank in collaboration with the African Union and the AfCFTA Secretariat, Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX WKND) is Africa’s premier event celebrating the continent’s creative and cultural industries. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora. Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan ,, KUMI , KWELAKU , and Galipette Atelier , highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion. The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026 , with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch . Bringing together 200 to 250 influential women leaders, policymakers, innovators, and international dignitaries, the high-level gathering will feature keynote addresses, strategic panels, and structured B2B networking aimed at fostering female leadership and economic empowerment across the continent. “We are thrilled to bring the African Woman 2.0 platform to Lagos alongside CANEX WKND 2026,” said Aïssata Sidibé N’DIA , Managing Director of RED Côte d’Ivoire / Afrique Femme. “This partnership offers an extraordinary opportunity to celebrate the ingenuity of African creative entrepreneurs, showcase Francophone fashion excellence on a global stage, and build lasting cross-border trade and investment synergies across Africa.” Event & Registration Details Dates: November 5–8, 2026 Venue: Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts (National Theatre), Lagos, Nigeria Registration: Delegate attendance at CANEX WKND 2026 is 100% free , but pre-registration is mandatory. sports.title: Red Sox News & Links: Will the Sox trade Franklin Arias this offseason?
sports.description: BINGHAMTON, NY - MAY 26: Franklin Arias #50 of the Portland Sea Dogs celebrates with teammates after defeating the Binghamton Rumble Ponies at Mirabito Stadium on Tuesday, May 26, 2026 in Binghamton, New York. (Photo by Kylie Richelle/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) As Matt laid out yesterday, there sure are a lot of rumors involving the Red Sox and shortstops, despite the fact that Franklin Arias is a shortstop with nothing left to prove in AAA. So what does that say about how the Sox view Arias? Maybe it doesn’t say anything than that they’re doing their due diligence. But here’s what the current dean of the Red Sox beat says about it in his offseason preview piece: “Some in the organization view Arias as almost untouchable.
